heading: Copy suppression partly compensates when earlier token-copying heads are ablated
definition: copy suppression is one mechanism of self-repair: when an upstream copier is ablated, there is less to suppress, which partly compensates.
summary: Independent studies support compensation by other components (“self-repair”) after ablating heads that copy names to the output (“name movers”) in GPT-2 small, with qualitative evidence in Pythia-160m. Evidence is limited to indirect object identification (IOI), which asks a model to identify a sentence’s recipient; independent tests do not isolate copy suppression as the compensating mechanism.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at <1B, IOI task only: GPT-2 small by two groups other than the original's, and Pythia-160m qualitatively. No tests at toy, 1-10B, 10-100B or >100B (counts: V4.studies_by_size has only the keys 'not stated' and '<1B'; the row subjects are GPT-2 small and Pythia-160m).
suggested_status.reason: arXiv:2608.19338 and arXiv:2610.02173 support V4 on GPT-2 small IOI with different causal methods. arXiv:2608.19338#r3 and arXiv:2608.19338#r4 use designed group ablations: interaction 1.830 and 1.681 with 95% CIs, code y, controls y. arXiv:2610.02173#r1 uses dosed swaps: L10.h7 γr −0.8864 ±SE 0.0211, code n, controls y. arXiv:2407.10827#selfrepair-160m reports reduced negativity after Name-Mover ablation qualitatively in Figure 4A for Pythia-160m at 300B tokens (no compensation magnitude or suppression-specific causal decomposition reported, controls n). Counts: V4.verdicts.supports.studies = 3, V4.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 0, V4.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0, V4.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0. V4.tested_by_review_class = {preprint: 3, workshop: 1} is the script's metadata; the checker identifies NeurIPS 2024 as the supplied arXiv:2407.10827 version's first-page venue header, so its workshop classification does not match that version and the assertion of no reviewed venue is withdrawn. The mechanistic and task caveats remain: no independent test checks that the compensation runs through copy suppression specifically (arXiv:2610.02173#r1 takes role labels from prior work), and all evidence is IOI name-mover ablation.
suggested_status.open_questions: Four results would change the level or its scope: (1) upstream-copier ablation outside IOI or across the training distribution; (2) a head-level test that the drop in suppression runs through the copy-suppression QK/OV mechanism; (3) a compensation fraction measured by an independent group; (4) any test at 1B parameters or more. A failed replication, or a credible argument that the apparent self-repair is an artifact of the ablation method, would move V4 toward C. arXiv:2610.02173 frames the effect as counterweight release, but its verdict is supports.

source.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding a Motif in Language Model Attention Heads
source.authors: Callum McDougall; Arthur Conmy; Cody Rushing; Thomas McGrath; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: The authors ablated three Name Mover Heads, which copy names to the output, in GPT-2 small during indirect object identification (IOI), a task asking for the recipient in a sentence.
original_result.result: Two heads that lower token logits (“Negative Heads”), L10H7 and L11H10, accounted for 39% of the compensation by later components after ablation (“downstream self-repair”). These heads attended more to tokens predicted by Name Mover Heads and decreased those tokens’ logits.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Pythia-160m: after name-mover (name-copying) heads were ablated, negative heads suppressed the answer less.
GPT-2-small: ablating main name-copying heads made negative heads suppress the answer less, partly compensating.
GPT-2 Small released L10.h7’s opposition as upstream copier signals were removed.

wording_issues.phrase: copy suppression is one mechanism of self-repair
wording_issues.issue: The independent tests show that negative heads' suppression or opposition falls when upstream name movers are removed. None checks that this is copy suppression. arXiv:2610.02173 measures a 'counterweight' slope for L10.h7 (γr −0.8864) and takes role labels from prior work (verdict fix on r1). Its title frames the effect as 'the Semblance of Self-Repair'. arXiv:2608.19338 measures a 2-head group E, not individual heads. arXiv:2407.10827 names head 9.5 a negative CS head from its component score and reports only reduced negativity.

wording_issues.phrase: when an upstream copier is ablated
wording_issues.issue: The statement has no task or model qualifier. Every result removes IOI Name Mover heads, and always as groups: the three Name Movers (arXiv:2310.04625 r14), P = 3 heads under mean or zero ablation (arXiv:2608.19338), the L9.h6 + L9.h9 pair under a dosed swap rather than deletion (arXiv:2610.02173), and Name-Mover heads in Pythia-160m (arXiv:2407.10827). No row removes a single copier, or any copier outside IOI.

method_sensitivity.what: In GPT-2-small IOI, the P × E interaction is 1.830 (95% CI [1.569, 2.076]) under mean ablation and 1.681 (95% CI [1.474, 1.889]) under zero ablation. Outside the rows: Δ(P+E) = −0.136 (mean) and −0.769 (zero), Sec. 5.5. The authors report that the direct interaction ordering persists across eight lexical/order conditions and both ablation types. The held-out predictive comparison uses one prompt template and mean ablation only. The sign is stable; magnitudes shift.

method_sensitivity.factor: which negative heads are held fixed (L10H7 and L11H10 back each other up)
method_sensitivity.what: Original: L11H10 backs up L10H7, and the loss increase is roughly twice as large when the L11H10 path is not controlled (Appendix C, Figure 12; not in rows). Its 39% self-repair share combines both heads (r14). In arXiv:2610.02173, including L10.h7 in the clamped core changes L11.h10's response from curved to nearly affine and increases the fitted coupling. So the attribution to one head depends on which other negative head is held fixed.

method_sensitivity.factor: reference convention and dose in dosed swaps
method_sensitivity.what: In GPT-2 Small IOI, under the alternative reference convention all ten reachable heads certify and held-out prediction is looser (median |z| = 0.41, §L.6); qualitative conclusions hold under both conventions. L10.h7 certifies but is strongly curved inside the dose window. The only two held-out class means beyond 2 SE are its λ=−½ points (§L.2). L11.h10 is the affine-law exception under the two-head core (R² = 0.413; |βr/γr| = 2.608, §L.3). The authors note that held-out dose tests interpolate rather than extrapolate. No numerical comparison of L10.h7 slopes across reference conventions is supplied.
